title: Ringed open extension, scalar restriction and normalized strict limits
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of arbitrary schemes, on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $T$, and use the restricted rings $R_U,S_U$ on the slice site $U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Write $r_V:\operatorname{Mod}(S_V)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_V)$ for scalar restriction, $V=U,T$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $J_R,J_S$ for sheafified ringed open extension [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The same letters denote exact termwise functors on complexes, strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and their unbounded derived categories [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].
There is a canonical natural isomorphism $e:r_TJ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}J_Rr_U$, induced by the identity of the underlying extension presheaves before abelian sheafification. It identifies the units and counits of the two open-extension/restriction adjunctions, on sheaves, complexes and derived strict towers.
Countable products of these pro-etale module sheaves are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Each $J_R,J_S$ has its invertible canonical product comparison, including the empty product; $r_U,r_T$ have the identity comparison on underlying abelian sheaves [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products]. Write $L_{V,R},L_{V,S}$ for total right derived inverse limit and, for any of these four functors $F$, use precisely the normalized comparison $\lambda_F:FL\xrightarrow{\sim}LF^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], with its signed Roos and K-injective resolution normalization. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(S_U))$ one has
$$L_{T,R}(e_M)\circ\lambda_{r_T,J_SM}\circ r_T(\lambda_{J_S,M})=\lambda_{J_R,r_UM}\circ J_R(\lambda_{r_U,M})\circ e_{L_{U,S}M}.$$
The equality is natural in derived strict-tower maps. The comparisons carry the canonical maps from every strict augmentation $\Delta C\to M$ to the corresponding maps after open extension and scalar restriction. Thus they identify quotient-tower completion units whenever $M$ is a quotient tower. No flatness of $a$, boundedness of $M$, or quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the ringed scalar/open comparison on the literal slice. Retain its sheafified direct-sum generator equation and unit/counit equations. The restriction comparison is the identity on underlying sections. Evaluate the unit/counit equations degreewise to obtain the complex equations, using the typed cbcComplexSquare wrapper. Recover the inverse mate from the unit equation, apply exact localization of inverse mates, and evaluate on the tower diagram category to obtain the derived-tower equations for the canonical square and adjunction.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 03DI, 03DJ; normalized Roos comparison as in the final blueprint comparison paragraph.

proof.text: For scalar restriction, reflect preservation of all products through the faithful forgetful functor to abelian sheaves; the composite is the unchanged underlying-sheaf functor. For both open extensions use their canonical product comparisons. Transfer preservation of products indexed in the coefficient universe to countable products using ULift and the induced equivalence of discrete categories. Ambient exact countable products follow from preservation of epimorphisms by the product functor. For the slice choose the reduced closed complement of the open, use the ringed open/closed adjunction with invertible unit, and transfer exact products from the ambient category along the fully faithful left adjoint.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 03DI, 03DJ; normalized Roos comparison as in the final blueprint comparison paragraph.

proof.text: Apply normalizedLimitSquareCoherence with corners Mod(S_U), Mod(S_T), Mod(R_U), Mod(R_T) and edges J_S, r_T, r_U, J_R. Use the four given total-right-derived functors and their units. This supplies the signed coordinate comparisons, the K-injective-normalized corners, their localization and conjugation equations, and the normalized square. The canonical wrappers cbcDerivedSquare, cbcDerivedTowerSquare and cbcDerivedTowerAdjunction denote the same existing constructions. Unpack the existential Coherence into its SquareData and SquareLaws; the normalized square is the sixth law, and all four comparisons come from that same fixed data.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 03DI, 03DJ; normalized Roos comparison as in the final blueprint comparison paragraph.

proof.text: Use the Grothendieck property of the four module categories and of their countable diagram categories (a separating family is given by left adjoints to evaluation). Extend each corner normalization from degreewise-injective K-injective complexes to every complex by naturality along the functorial K-injective resolution; cancel the invertible Roos image of the resolution map. The signed coordinate formula for each comparison sends the ordinary-limit inclusion to the corresponding inclusion: check the first coordinate by every product projection and the second coordinate is zero. Descend this equality through the localization factorization and conjugation equations to obtain all four CbcLimitNormalized equations. Each augmentation is the ordinary-limit equation precomposed with the map induced by its cone. Factorization naturality and the limit universal property give all four augmentation equations. Combine these with the normalized square supplied in the preceding step.
